389	### Expressions
390	
391	#### C# Expressions (`expressionLanguage: CSharp`)
392	
393	Applies to XAML workflow files in projects whose `project.json` has `expressionLanguage: CSharp`. These rules govern expressions inside XAML — they are unrelated to coded workflows (`.cs` files), which are plain C# and do not use `CSharpValue` / `CSharpReference` elements.
394	
395	Expressions use explicit `<CSharpValue>` (for read/evaluate) or `<CSharpReference>` (for write/lvalue) elements inside `<InArgument>` / `<OutArgument>`:
396	```xml
397	<Assign DisplayName="Set Name">
398	  <Assign.To>
399	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
400	      <CSharpReference x:TypeArguments="x:String">fullName</CSharpReference>
401	    </OutArgument>
402	  </Assign.To>
403	  <Assign.Value>
404	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
405	      <CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">firstName + " " + lastName</CSharpValue>
406	    </InArgument>
407	  </Assign.Value>
408	</Assign>
409	```
410	
411	**Important**: Do NOT use `[bracket]` shorthand for expressions. Brackets create `VisualBasicValue` nodes at deserialization time, causing validation failures for C#-only syntax (`null`, `?.`, `??`, `typeof()`, etc.).
412	
413	**Stronger rule for attribute-form bindings on `InArgument<T>` / `OutArgument<T>`:** in XAML projects with `expressionLanguage: CSharp`, any **non-literal** attribute value (`Message="variableName"`, `Text=""Hello " + name"`) is also deserialized as a `VisualBasicValue<T>` and fails at runtime with `JIT compilation is disabled for non-Legacy projects`. The attribute parser defaults to VB regardless of the project's expression language. Use `<CSharpValue>` / `<CSharpReference>` child elements for anything that isn't a plain literal. See [csharp-expression-pitfalls.md](csharp-expression-pitfalls.md) and [csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](csharp-activity-binding-guide.md).
414	
415	**Safe attribute-form values** (no expression evaluator involved, type converter handles them directly):
416	- Literal strings on `InArgument<String>`: `Text="Book trip"`, `DisplayName="Open file"`
417	- Enums: `Level="Info"`, `ClickType="Single"`, `MouseButton="Left"`
418	- Numbers, booleans, `{x:Null}`
419	- `TimeSpan` literals: `Duration="00:00:02"`
420	
421	**For activity-specific recipes** (`LogMessage.Message` as `InArgument<Object>`, `NGetText.TextString` as `OutArgument<String>`, `StartProcess.FileName` with composed paths, `Assign`, `If.Condition`, etc.), see [csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](csharp-activity-binding-guide.md). That file is the canonical lookup for the binding form per common activity property.
422	
423	#### VB Expressions (`expressionLanguage: VisualBasic`)
424	Expressions use VB syntax with `[bracket]` shorthand (VB is the default deserialization target for brackets):
425	```xml
426	<InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">[firstName & " " & lastName]</InArgument>
427	```
428	
429	**Check `project.json` `expressionLanguage` field to determine which syntax to use.**
430	
431	### Resource Types (IResource / ILocalResource)
432	
433	Some activity properties accept `IResource` or `ILocalResource` types instead of plain strings for file inputs. These are part of UiPath's resource abstraction model:
434	
435	| Type | Description | When Used |
436	|------|-------------|-----------|
437	| `IResource` | Generic resource (local file, remote file, cloud attachment) | Activities that accept any file source |
438	| `ILocalResource` | Local file on disk (has `LocalPath` property) | Activities that need a file on the local filesystem |
439	| `IRemoteResource` | Remote resource with a URI and a local copy | Cloud/API-sourced files |
440	
441	**In XAML**, resource-typed properties are typically set via expressions that create the resource:
442	```xml
443	<!-- LocalResource from a file path (C# expression) -->
444	<InArgument x:TypeArguments="upr:ILocalResource">
445	  <CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="upr:ILocalResource">LocalResource.FromPath(filePath)</CSharpValue>
446	</InArgument>
447	```
448	
449	Required namespace for resource types:
450	```xml
451	<x:String>UiPath.Platform.ResourceHandling</x:String>
452	```
453	
454	**Activity Storage**: Some activities use a bucket-based storage system (`.storage/` folder in the project). Resources stored at design-time in `.storage/.runtime/<bucket>/` are packed into the published NuPkg and available at runtime. This is managed automatically — you don't need to edit storage resources directly in XAML.

720	## Property Binding: Attributes vs Child Elements
721	
722	XAML properties can be set in two ways: as XML attributes or as child elements. Both are valid XAML, but some properties only work reliably in one form.
723	
724	### Attribute Syntax (Inline)
725	```xml
726	<ui:LogMessage Message="[myVar]" Level="Info" />
727	```
728	
729	### Child Element Syntax (Property Element)
730	```xml
731	<ui:SomeActivity>
732	  <ui:SomeActivity.Result>
733	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">[outputVar]</OutArgument>
734	  </ui:SomeActivity.Result>
735	</ui:SomeActivity>
736	```
737	
738	### When to Use Which
739	
740	**Simple values** (strings, enums, booleans, VB expressions in brackets) almost always work as attributes:
741	```xml
742	DisplayName="My Activity" Message="[variable]" Level="Info"
743	```
744	
745	**Output properties** (`OutArgument`, `Result`) may require child element syntax. Some activities accept `Result="[var]"` as an attribute; others only work with the expanded child element form. If an attribute-form output binding causes a validation error, try the child element form.
746	
747	**Complex objects** (BackupSlot, MailboxArgument, ActivityAction, dictionaries) always require child element syntax — they cannot be expressed as a single attribute value.
748	
749	**Strings containing literal `[` or `]`** (e.g., UIA special-key tokens like `[k(enter)]`, `[d(ctrl)]`, `[u(ctrl)]`) require child element syntax. The attribute form `Foo="["…[k(enter)]"]"` runs correctly because the runtime VB compiler reads quoted string literals correctly, but the literal brackets inside the string collide with the outer `[ … ]` VB expression markers and the value will not render in Studio. See [common-pitfalls.md § NTypeInto `Text` with literal `[k(...)]` special-key tokens](common-pitfalls.md#ntypeinto-text-with-literal-k-special-key-tokens).
750	
751	### Version-Sensitive Properties
752	
753	Properties may exist in one package version but not another. If `validate` reports "Could not find member 'PropertyName'":
754	1. The property may not exist in the installed package version — remove it
755	2. The property may have been renamed between versions — check examples from the same package version
756	3. Use `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output as the authoritative set of properties for the installed version
757	
758	## ConnectorActivity Internals
759	
760	Understanding the structure of `isactr:ConnectorActivity` so you know what you can and cannot edit.
761	
762	### Properties (What They Are)
763	
764	| Property | Editable? | Description |
765	|----------|-----------|-------------|
766	| `Configuration` | **NEVER** | ZIP-compressed, Base64-encoded JSON blob containing the full activity schema (fields, types, connector metadata). This is obtained and computed for you using the `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` command. Do not parse, modify, or construct manually. |
767	| `ConnectionId` | Yes (replace GUID) | Integration Service connection GUID. Use `uip is connections list [connector-key]` to discover available connections and their IDs. |
768	| `UiPathActivityTypeId` | **NEVER** | Identifies the specific connector operation. Obtain using `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` or `uip rpa activities find`. |
769	| `DisplayName` | Yes | Human-readable activity name for the designer. |
770	
771	### FieldObjects (Input/Output Interface)
772	
773	`FieldObjects` is the collection of input and output fields. Each `isactr:FieldObject` has:
774	
775	| Attribute | Description |
776	|-----------|-------------|
777	| `Name` | Field identifier (maps to the connector API parameter). Must match exactly what `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` returns. |
778	| `Type` | One of: `FieldArgument` (contains an Activity Argument), `FieldLiteral` (contains a literal value), `FilterTreeValue` (filter builder criteria), `None` (empty). |
779	
780	**What you CAN edit in FieldObjects:**
781	- **Input field values**: Change the `InArgument` value inside a `FieldObject.Value` to set different input data (e.g., change a search query string).
782	- **Bind to variables**: Replace a literal value with a variable reference using `<CSharpValue>` (e.g., `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">myVariable</CSharpValue>`).
783	
784	**What you CANNOT edit:**
785	- Field `Name` values — these must match the connector API schema exactly.
786	- Field `Type` values — these are determined by the connector metadata.
787	- Output field structure — the `OutArgument` types reference JIT-generated assemblies.
788	- Adding/removing FieldObjects — the set of fields comes from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`.
789	
790	### JIT-Generated Assemblies
791	
792	Output fields often use types from JIT-compiled assemblies with hashed names:
793	```
794	CDF573A04A6_search_r.VeKd1XI2qK1X56UO2Br3Ui3
795	^connection(last10)   ^operation   ^content hash
796	```
797	
798	These assembly names are:
799	- **Unpredictable** — derived from SHA-512 hashes of the type schema
800	- **Connection-specific** — different connections produce different hashes
801	- **Generated by the runtime** — you cannot create or reference them without `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`
802	
803	The corresponding namespace imports and assembly references MUST come from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output. Never construct them.
804	
805	### What `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` Returns for Dynamic Activities
806	
807	When you call `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` with `isDynamicActivity: true`, it returns everything needed:
808	1. The complete `<isactr:ConnectorActivity>` XAML element with `Configuration` blob, `UiPathActivityTypeId`, and `FieldObjects`
809	2. All required `xmlns` declarations for the root `<Activity>` element
810	3. All required namespace imports and references
811	
812	Use this output as-is. The only things you should modify are:
813	- `DisplayName` — set a meaningful name
814	- `ConnectionId` — if swapping to a different connection of the same connector type
815	- Input `FieldObject` values — to set the actual data for your workflow

251	  <Assign.To>
252	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
253	      <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter" />
254	    </OutArgument>
255	  </Assign.To>
256	  <Assign.Value>
257	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
258	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter + 1" />
259	    </InArgument>
260	  </Assign.Value>
261	</Assign>
262	```
263	
264	**Notes:** Prefer the generic `Assign<T>` form — typed args surface mismatch errors at `validate` time. `To` must be a writable expression (variable, argument, indexer) — Studio's emitter uses `VisualBasicReference` (or `CSharpReference` in C# projects) for the writable side and `VisualBasicValue` (or `CSharpValue`) for the readable side. One `Assign` per target — no multi-target form.
265

270	### Log Message
271	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.LogMessage`
272	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`; no extra prefix needed (`x:Object` uses the root `xmlns:x`).
273	
274	**Snippet:**
275	```xml
276	<ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Message">
277	  <ui:LogMessage.Message>
278	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
279	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Processed {count} items"" />

285	**Non-obvious properties:**
286	- `Level` — `InArgument<LogLevel>` — required-in-practice; **default `Info`** but the skip-tax hides it from `get-default-xaml`. Enum values: `Trace` | `Info` | `Warn` | `Error` | `Fatal`.
287	- `Message` — `InArgument<object>` — **not** `string`. Accepts any expression; the activity calls `.ToString()`. In VB projects, bracket shorthand can hold composite expressions such as `[$"x = {x}"]`; in C# projects, use `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object">...</CSharpValue>`.
288	
289	**Notes:** Prefer `LogMessage` over `WriteLine` for any output that must appear in Orchestrator. `Level` defaults to `Info`; omit only when you want `Info` and the explicit attribute clutters the snippet.

317	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Delay`
318	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the `TimeSpan` argument type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).

320	**Snippet:**

322	<Delay DisplayName="Delay">
323	  <Delay.Duration>

326	    </InArgument>
327	  </Delay.Duration>

In VB projects, bracket shorthand such as `[TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)]` is valid; in C# projects, use `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="s:TimeSpan">TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)</CSharpValue>` or a literal attribute such as `Duration="00:00:05"`. Blocks the workflow thread for the full duration — avoid inside `ForEach`/`While` bodies where it multiplies. Do **not** use `Delay` to wait on external state; use `RetryScope`, `WaitForElement`, or a polling loop with a `Condition` instead.

1	# Trigger Pattern Guide
2	
3	Authoring and editing trigger workflows in XAML. Covers placement, lifecycle, `ui:TriggerScope` handling, and verification.
4	
5	## Two Trigger Types
6	
7	`uip rpa activities find` returns `isTrigger` and `triggerType` on every trigger activity. `triggerType` is the type discriminator.
8	
9	### Integration triggers (`triggerType: "integration"`) — strict placement
10	
11	- **MUST be the first activity** of `Main.xaml`'s root `Sequence`.
12	- **CANNOT be placed inside `ui:TriggerScope`.**
13	- **Connection asset:** required for IS-based triggers (Mail, GSuite, O365, Salesforce, Jira, Slack, ServiceNow, any `*.IntegrationService.Activities` package). Not required for Orchestrator-native triggers (`TimeTrigger`, `QueueTrigger`, `ManualTrigger`).
14	- **Runtime behavior:** the activity is an **unwrap routine**. Orchestrator (or the IS webhook layer) holds the subscription, dispatches a fresh job per event, and injects event payload context. The activity's `Execute` reads that context — e.g., `NewEmailReceived.ExecuteWithRetryAsync` reads `UiPathEventObjectId`, then calls `GraphServiceClient.GetEmailByIdAsync(...)` to fetch the email. It does not poll, watch, or listen.
15	- **Examples:** `NewEmailReceived` (O365 Outlook, GSuite Gmail), `NewFileCreated`, `NewEventCreated`, `NewEventInvitationReceived`, `RowAddedToSheetBottom`, SharePoint list-item triggers, every IS connector trigger (Salesforce / Jira / Slack / ServiceNow / Microsoft Teams CRUD events), `TimeTrigger`, `QueueTrigger`, `ManualTrigger`.
16	
17	### Local triggers (`triggerType: "local"`) — flexible placement
18	
19	- Place EITHER:
20	  - As the first activity of `Main.xaml`'s root `Sequence` → Orchestrator dispatches a fresh job per event (entry-point semantics).
21	  - Inside `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>`, handler in `<ui:TriggerScope.Action>` → the robot stays alive while the scope is active; the trigger fires in-process.
22	- The placement choice is a runtime-model decision (per-event jobs vs long-running robot). Both are valid.
23	- **Connection asset:** not required.
24	- **Runtime behavior:** the activity is a real in-process subscriber. `StartMonitor` installs the listener (e.g. `FileChangeTriggerV3` → `FileSystemWatcher` + a background event-loop `Task` in `UiPath.Core.Activities.FileWatcher`); events flow through `TriggerScope`'s bookmark queue when wrapped, or through entry-point dispatch when placed at root.
25	- **Examples:** `FileChangeTriggerV3`, `RepeatTrigger`, `GlobalVariableChangedTrigger`, UIA Next triggers (`NClickTrigger`, `NKeyboardTrigger`), classic UIA V2 triggers (`ClickTriggerV2`, `ClickImageTriggerV2`, `KeyPressTriggerV2`, `ElementStateChangeTrigger`, `ElementAttributeChangeTrigger`, `MouseTriggerV2`, `HotkeyTriggerV2`, `SystemTriggerV2`, `SapSessionTrigger`), `AppRequestTrigger`.
26	
27	Integration triggers never go inside `ui:TriggerScope`. Local triggers have no equivalent restriction — both placements are valid.
28	
29	## Decision Rule
30	
31	1. Run `uip rpa activities find --query "<event keyword>" --output json`. Read `isTrigger` and `triggerType`.
32	2. Branch on the CLI signal:
33	   - **Both fields absent** → regular activity, not a trigger.
34	   - **`isTrigger: true`, `triggerType: "integration"`** → integration trigger. **Place as the first activity of root `Sequence`; never inside `ui:TriggerScope`.** Check connection requirement — IS-based packages (Mail/GSuite/O365/`*.IntegrationService.Activities`) need a `ConnectionId`; `TimeTrigger`/`QueueTrigger`/`ManualTrigger` do not.
35	   - **`isTrigger: true`, `triggerType: "local"`** → local trigger. **Choose placement** based on runtime model — first activity of root for per-event dispatch, inside `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>` for long-running in-process subscription. No connection asset.
36	   - **`isTrigger: true`, unknown `triggerType`** → unknown category (forward-compat — new flavors may appear). Read the bundled doc and ask the user if still ambiguous.
37	3. For trigger activities, read **both** docs (per SKILL.md Rule 21): the bundled `references/activity-docs/<packageName>/<closest-version>/activities/<ClassNameTail>.md` **and** the project-local `{PROJECT_DIR}/.local/docs/packages/<packageName>/activities/<ClassNameTail>.md` if present. The bundled doc carries placement guidance, deployment context, and cross-cutting namespace/assembly gotchas the auto-generated `.local/docs` extractor omits; the `.local/docs` version reflects the exact installed package version. Also read the package's bundled `overview.md`.
38	
39	## Entry-Point Worked Example — Office 365 New Email Received
40	
41	A workflow that fires when an Outlook email arrives in INBOX with attachments.
42	
43	```xml
44	<Activity mc:Ignorable="sap sap2010" x:Class="Main"
45	    xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
46	    xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
47	    xmlns:sap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities/presentation"
48	    xmlns:sap2010="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/presentation"
49	    xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"
50	    xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"
51	    xmlns:umamt="clr-namespace:UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities.Mail.Triggers;assembly=UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities"
52	    xmlns:umm="clr-namespace:UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Models;assembly=UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365"
53	    xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml">
54	  <Sequence DisplayName="Main Sequence">
55	    <Sequence.Variables>
56	      <Variable x:TypeArguments="umm:Office365Message" Name="email" />
57	    </Sequence.Variables>
58	
59	    <umamt:NewEmailReceived
60	        DisplayName="New Email Received"
61	        ConnectionId="<CONNECTION_GUID>"
62	        UseConnectionService="True"
63	        AuthScopesInvalid="False"
64	        BrowserFolderId="INBOX"
65	        BrowserFolderName="Inbox"
66	        FilterExpression="(parentFolderId=='INBOX')&&(hasAttachments==`true`)"
67	        IncludeAttachments="True"
68	        MarkAsRead="True"
69	        WithAttachmentsOnly="True"
70	        Result="[email]" />
71	
72	    <!-- Handler: rest of the Sequence acts on `email` -->
73	    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" Message="["Got email from " + email.From.Address]" />
74	  </Sequence>
75	</Activity>
76	```
77	
78	Three critical shape rules:
79	
80	1. The trigger is the **first child** of the root `Sequence`. There is no `ui:TriggerScope` wrapping it.
81	2. `Result="[email]"` binds the activity's `Office365Message` output to a workflow-scope variable. The rest of the `Sequence` is the handler.
82	3. `FilterExpression` runs **server-side** (free) before the trigger fires — never re-implement the filter as an `If` inside the handler. Boolean literals use backticks; AND uses XML-escaped `&&`. Full syntax: [activity-docs/UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities/3.8/activities/NewEmailReceived.md](activity-docs/UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities/3.8/activities/NewEmailReceived.md).
83	
84	## Local Trigger Worked Example — UI Click
85	
86	A workflow that runs while a desktop app is open and reacts to clicks. The exact `xmlns` prefix and args type vary by package — always start from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml --activity-class-name <FullClassName>` rather than hand-writing the namespace.
87	
88	Structural shape (placeholders in angle brackets — fill from `get-default-xaml`):
89	
90	```xml
91	<Activity x:Class="Main" ...>
92	  <Sequence DisplayName="Main Sequence">
93	    <ui:TriggerScope DisplayName="Trigger Scope"
94	                     SchedulingMode="Sequential"
95	                     xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities">
96	      <ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>
97	        <!-- One or more local trigger activities. Get full XAML via:
98	               uip rpa activities get-default-xaml \
99	                 --activity-class-name <FullClassName> \
100	                 --project-dir "<PROJECT_DIR>" --output json -->
101	        <<TriggerPrefix>:<TriggerClassName> DisplayName="..." ... />
102	      </ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>
103	      <ui:TriggerScope.Action>
104	        <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="<TriggerArgsType>">
105	          <Sequence>
106	            <!-- handler -->
107	          </Sequence>
108	        </ActivityAction>
109	      </ui:TriggerScope.Action>
110	    </ui:TriggerScope>
111	  </Sequence>
112	</Activity>
113	```
114	
115	Shape rules:
116	
117	1. `ui:TriggerScope` (`UiPath.Core.Activities.TriggerScope`, in package `UiPath.System.Activities`) is the container. `Triggers` is a collection — one or more child trigger activities.
118	2. `ui:TriggerScope.Action` is the handler. It is an `ActivityAction` typed on the trigger's args type (e.g. `MonitorClickEventArgs` for `NClickTrigger`, `FileSystemArgs` for file-change variants). Use `get-default-xaml` on the trigger to discover the exact args type.
119	3. **`SchedulingMode`** controls handler queueing (source: `Triggers/TriggerScope.cs`):
120	   - `Concurrent` — fire all handler instances in parallel.
121	   - `Sequential` *(default in most templates)* — queue events; run one handler at a time in arrival order. Filterable triggers can drop duplicate queued events.
122	   - `SequentialCollapse` — sequential, but collapse repeated events to the latest.
123	   - `SequentialDrop` — sequential, but cancel the running handler when a new event arrives.
124	   - `OneTime` — fire once and cancel the scope's child triggers.
125	4. **`ContinueOnError`** — when `true`, a faulted handler logs and the scope keeps running. When `false` (default), a fault stops the scope.
126	5. **`Break`** activity (from `UiPath.System.Activities`) inside the handler exits the `TriggerScope` cleanly.
127	6. The job remains alive for as long as `TriggerScope` is active. This is the wrong choice for events that arrive over hours/days; place the trigger at the workflow root instead, so Orchestrator owns the subscription and dispatches per event.
128	
129	## Reading and Editing Existing TriggerScope XAML
130	
131	Existing projects routinely use `ui:TriggerScope`. When you encounter one, treat it as a valid local-trigger pattern — do not flatten it. The choice between scoped and root placement for a local trigger is a runtime-model decision (long-running robot vs per-event jobs); changing it without the user's intent is wrong.
132	
133	**How to identify:** any XAML containing `<ui:TriggerScope ...>` is a local-trigger workflow. The robot is expected to stay alive while this scope is active.
134	
135	**Safe edits:**
136	
137	- Adding another local trigger to the same scope → append to `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>`. Confirm the new trigger's args type matches (or the scope's `Action` `x:TypeArguments` is the common base — typically `TriggerArgs`). Integration triggers cannot be added here.
138	- Modifying the handler → edit inside `<ui:TriggerScope.Action>`. Do not move handler activities outside the scope.
139	- Changing `SchedulingMode` → safe; pick from the values above. Default unset value behaves as `Sequential`.
140	
141	**Unsafe edits — these break the workflow:**
142	
143	- Moving a local trigger out of `ui:TriggerScope` to root placement when the user only asked you to "modernize" the workflow. The two placements have different deployment models (per-event jobs vs long-running robot); ask the user first.
144	- Removing `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>` while keeping `<ui:TriggerScope.Action>` — `CacheMetadata` validation fails (`TriggerScope_NoTrigger`).
145	- Inserting an integration trigger (`triggerType: "integration"`) inside `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>` — see [Anti-patterns](#anti-patterns).
146	
147	**When to question a TriggerScope you find:** if `<ui:TriggerScope.Triggers>` contains an activity whose bundled doc labels it **Integration trigger** (e.g. `NewEmailReceived`, `TimeTrigger`, `QueueTrigger`), the prior author placed an integration trigger inside a `TriggerScope`. The workflow compiles but does not get registered as an Orchestrator trigger. Flag this to the user — the fix is to move that trigger to the workflow root.
148

178	## Connection Handling (IS Triggers)
179	
180	Integration triggers from Integration Service packages require a `ConnectionId`. A placeholder GUID (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`) passes `uip rpa validate` and `uip rpa build` but fails at runtime when Orchestrator tries to subscribe. Resolve a real connection scoped to the connector and across all folders (active-folder-only scans miss connections owned by other folders):
181	
182	```bash
183	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
184	```
185	
186	For example, `uip is connections list "uipath-microsoft-outlook365" --all-folders --output json` for the O365 Mail triggers. Copy the connection's GUID into `ConnectionId`. If no connection exists, create one (`uip is connections create <connector-key>`) and verify it's active (`uip is connections ping <connection-id>`).
187	
188	## Server-Side Filtering
189	
190	Integration triggers from IS packages typically expose a filter property — an OData-style boolean predicate (or structured tree) that runs on the connector side **before** the trigger fires. Use it for any "fire only if X" logic. Re-implementing the filter inside the handler wastes Orchestrator dispatch and robot time on events you would discard.
191	
192	Per-package conventions (read each package's bundled `overview.md` for canonical syntax):
193	
194	- **O365 Mail** (`umm:` prefix family): `FilterExpression` as a string attribute. OData-like: `(parentFolderId=='INBOX')`, `(hasAttachments==`true`)`. AND uses `&&`; booleans use backticks. See [activity-docs/UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities/3.8/activities/overview.md](activity-docs/UiPath.MicrosoftOffice365.Activities/3.8/activities/overview.md).
195	- **GSuite Gmail**: `Filter` as a structured child element with `LogicalOperator` + `Criteria` leaves, not a string. See [activity-docs/UiPath.GSuite.Activities/3.8/activities/NewEmailReceived.md](activity-docs/UiPath.GSuite.Activities/3.8/activities/NewEmailReceived.md).
196	- **IS connector triggers** (Salesforce, Jira, Slack, …): authored as a structured filter tree, not a string. Discover the filterable field names via `uip is triggers describe "<connector>" "<OPERATION>" "<object>" --output json` → read `Data.FilterFields[*].Name`. The CLI compiles the tree into the runtime expression; do not pass the compiled form directly.
197	
198	## Lifecycle and Verification
199	
200	Lifecycle depends on placement, not type. Two paths:
201	
202	### Entry-point lifecycle (trigger at workflow root)
203	
204	Applies to all integration triggers, and to local triggers placed at root.
205	
206	1. **Author** — place trigger as the first activity of root `Sequence`, bind output to variable, write handler. Per-file `validate` clean.
207	2. **Build** — `uip rpa build "<PROJECT_DIR>" --output json` clean.
208	3. **Publish** — `.nupkg` to Orchestrator (see [publishing-guide.md](publishing-guide.md)). On publish, Orchestrator detects the trigger from the workflow's activity registration and exposes it as a Process/Time/Queue Trigger candidate.
209	
210	**`uip rpa run` is NOT a meaningful smoke test for entry-point triggers.** The CLI executes the workflow once in-process, which does not exercise Orchestrator subscription or the connector's webhook/polling lifecycle. A clean `run` only proves the handler XAML compiles and the trigger activity can be instantiated.
211	
212	### In-process lifecycle (local trigger inside `ui:TriggerScope`)
213	
214	Applies only to local triggers wrapped in `ui:TriggerScope`.
215	
216	1. **Author** — `ui:TriggerScope` with `Triggers` (one or more local trigger activities) and `Action` (the handler). Per-file `validate` clean.
217	2. **Build** — `uip rpa build` clean.
218	3. **Run** — `uip rpa run --file-path Main.xaml --project-dir "<PROJECT_DIR>" --output json`. The robot stays alive; trigger events fire while the run is active. Generate an event (click, file change, etc.) and confirm the handler executes.
219	4. **Deploy** — publish to Orchestrator and start as a long-running attended/unattended job. The job remains active and consumes a robot slot for the duration.
220	
221	## Anti-patterns
222	
223	1. **Integration trigger wrapped in `ui:TriggerScope`.** Re-author by removing the `ui:TriggerScope` wrapper and placing the trigger at the root.
224	2. **Re-implementing the filter as an `If` in the handler.** Robot pays dispatch cost on every event the filter would have rejected. Move the predicate into the trigger's filter property.
225	3. **Calling `uip rpa run` to "test" an O365/Gmail/Salesforce/queue/schedule trigger.** See entry-point lifecycle above — `run` does not exercise Orchestrator subscription.
226	4. **Moving a local trigger out of `ui:TriggerScope` to root placement without intent.** Both placements are valid for local triggers; the choice is a runtime-model decision (per-event jobs vs long-running robot). Confirm with the user before changing it.
227	5. **Hand-editing the auto-generated `.local/docs/.../<Trigger>.md`.** That file is regenerated on package restore. Treat it as read-only; the bundled doc in `references/activity-docs/` is the editable source of placement and example guidance.
228	6. **Inventing an `xmlns:` prefix for an unfamiliar trigger.** Always pull the namespace from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml --activity-class-name <FullClassName>`; do not infer it from the class's logical hierarchy.

1	# Get IMAP Email List
2	
3	`UiPath.Mail.IMAP.Activities.GetIMAPMailMessages`
4	
5	Retrieves an IMAP email message from a specified server.
6	
7	**Package:** `UiPath.Mail.Activities`
8	**Category:** Mail.IMAP
9	**Platform:** Cross-platform
10	
11	## Properties
12	
13	### Input
14	
15	| Name | Display Name | Kind | Type | Required | Default | Description |
16	|------|-------------|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
17	| Server | Server | InArgument | string | No | | The hostname or IP address of the IMAP mail server (e.g., "imap.gmail.com"). |
18	| Port | Port | InArgument | int | No | | The port number used to connect to the IMAP server (e.g., 993 for SSL/TLS connections). |
19	| MailFolder | Mail folder | InArgument | string | No | `"Inbox"` | The name of the mail folder from which to retrieve messages (e.g., "Inbox", "Sent"). |
20	| Email | Email | InArgument | string | No | | The email address used to authenticate with the IMAP server. |
21	| Password | Password | InArgument | string | No | | The plain text password for IMAP server authentication. Mutually exclusive with SecurePassword. |
22	| SecurePassword | Secure password | InArgument | SecureString | No | | The password as a SecureString for IMAP server authentication. Mutually exclusive with Password. |
23	| UseOAuth | Use OAuth | InArgument | bool | No | | Whether to use OAuth 2.0 authentication instead of basic username/password credentials. |
24	| ClientName | Client name | InArgument | string | No | | An optional client application name sent to the IMAP server during the identification handshake. |
25	| ClientVersion | Client version | InArgument | string | No | | An optional client application version string sent to the IMAP server during the identification handshake. |
26	| Top | Top | InArgument | int | No | `30` | The maximum number of messages to retrieve. |
27	| TimeoutMS | TimeoutMS | InArgument | int | No | | The maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the mail server to respond before timing out. |
28	| FilterExpression | FilterExpression | InArgument | string | No | | An IMAP search filter expression using IMAP SEARCH command syntax (e.g., `SUBJECT "test" FROM "user@example.com"`). |
29	| FilterExpressionCharacterSet | FilterExpressionCharacterSet | InArgument | string | No | `"UTF-8"` | The character set used to encode the IMAP filter expression. |
30	| DeleteMessages | DeleteMessages | InArgument | bool | No | | When true, messages are deleted from the server after being retrieved. |
31	| OnlyUnreadMessages | Only unread messages | InArgument | bool | No | `true` | When true, only unread (unseen) messages are retrieved. |
32	| MarkAsRead | Mark as read | InArgument | bool | No | | When true, retrieved messages are marked as read on the server. |
33	| IgnoreCRL | Ignore CRL | InArgument | bool | No | `false` | When true, skips certificate revocation list (CRL) checking during SSL/TLS connections. |
34	
35	### Configuration
36	
37	| Name | Display Name | Type | Default | Description |
38	|------|-------------|------|---------|-------------|
39	| OrderByDate | OrderByDate | EOrderByDate | `NewestFirst` | Specifies the sort order of retrieved messages by date. |
40	| SecureConnection | Secure connection | SecureSocketEncryption | `Auto` | Specifies the type of SSL/TLS encryption to use when connecting to the IMAP server. |
41	
42	### Output
43	
44	| Name | Display Name | Type | Description |
45	|------|-------------|------|-------------|
46	| Messages | Messages | List<[MailMessage](types/MailMessage.md)> | The output collection of retrieved [MailMessage](types/MailMessage.md) objects. Each [MailMessage](types/MailMessage.md) contains the email's sender, recipients, subject, body, and attachments. |
47	
48	## XAML Example
49	
50	```xml
51	<imap:GetIMAPMailMessages
52	    DisplayName="Get IMAP Email List"
53	    Server="imap.gmail.com"
54	    Port="993"
55	    Email="user@example.com"
56	    Password="password"
57	    MailFolder="Inbox"
58	    OnlyUnreadMessages="True"
59	    MarkAsRead="False"
60	    Top="30"
61	    OrderByDate="NewestFirst"
62	    SecureConnection="Auto"
63	    Messages="[emailMessages]" />
64	```
65	
66	## Notes
67	
68	- Inherits from `GetMailActivity`, which provides the `Top`, `TimeoutMS`, and `Messages` properties.
69	- `Password` and `SecurePassword` belong to mutually exclusive overload groups; provide only one.
70	- The `EnableSSL` property exists but is not browsable (hidden from the designer); use `SecureConnection` instead.
71	- The `FilterExpression` uses IMAP SEARCH command syntax, not LINQ or SQL-like queries.
72	- Related activities: `MoveIMAPMailMessageToFolder`, `DeleteImapMailMessage`, `NewIMAPEmailReceivedTrigger`.

18	| MailFolder | Mail folder | InArgument | string | No | | The destination folder to move the message to (e.g., "Archive", "Important"). |
19	| FromFolder | FromFolder | InArgument | string | No | | The source folder from which to move the message. Required to locate the message on the server. |
20	| Server | Server | InArgument | string | No | | The hostname or IP address of the IMAP mail server. |
21	| Port | Port | InArgument | int | No | | The port number used to connect to the IMAP server. |

24	| SecurePassword | Secure password | InArgument | SecureString | No | | The password as a SecureString for IMAP server authentication. Mutually exclusive with Password. |
25	| UseOAuth | Use OAuth | InArgument | bool | No | | Whether to use OAuth 2.0 authentication instead of basic credentials. |
26	| ClientName | ClientName | InArgument | string | No | | An optional client application name sent to the IMAP server during identification. |
27	| ClientVersion | ClientVersion | InArgument | string | No | | An optional client application version string sent to the IMAP server during identification. |
28	| IgnoreCRL | Ignore CRL | InArgument | bool | No | `false` | When true, skips certificate revocation list (CRL) checking during SSL/TLS connections. |
29	
30	### Configuration
31	
32	| Name | Display Name | Type | Default | Description |
33	|------|-------------|------|---------|-------------|
34	| EnableSSL | EnableSSL | bool | `true` | Indicates whether to use SSL when connecting to the IMAP server. Deprecated in favor of SecureConnection. |
35	| SecureConnection | Secure connection | SecureSocketEncryption | `Auto` | Specifies the type of SSL/TLS encryption to use when connecting to the IMAP server. |
36	
37	### Output
38	
39	This activity has no output properties.
40	
41	## XAML Example
42	
43	```xml
44	<imap:MoveIMAPMailMessageToFolder
45	    DisplayName="Move IMAP Email"
46	    Server="imap.gmail.com"
47	    Port="993"
48	    Email="user@example.com"
49	    Password="password"
50	    MailMessage="[emailMessage]"
51	    FromFolder="Inbox"
52	    MailFolder="Archive"
53	    SecureConnection="Auto" />
54	```

56	## Notes
57	
58	- The `MailMessage` property is validated at design time; a validation error is raised if it has no expression set. See [MailMessage](types/MailMessage.md).
59	- `Password` and `SecurePassword` belong to mutually exclusive overload groups; provide only one.

<Activity mc:Ignorable="sap sap2010" x:Class="Workflows_ClassifyEmail"
  mva:VisualBasic.Settings="{x:Null}"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
  xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
  xmlns:mva="clr-namespace:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities;assembly=System.Activities"
  xmlns:sap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sap2010="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=mscorlib"
  xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"
  xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml">
  <x:Members>
    <x:Property Name="in_Subject" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_Body" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="out_Category" Type="OutArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="out_Priority" Type="OutArgument(x:String)" />
  </x:Members>
  <TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="x:String">
      <x:String>System.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Statements</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Expressions</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Validation</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.XamlIntegration</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections.Generic</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections.ObjectModel</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Data</x:String>
      <x:String>System.IO</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Linq</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Core</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Core.Activities</x:String>
    </sco:Collection>
  </TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
  <TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="AssemblyReference">
      <AssemblyReference>System.Activities</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>Microsoft.VisualBasic</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Private.CoreLib</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>mscorlib</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Linq</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Data</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Data.Common</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Core</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>UiPath.System.Activities</AssemblyReference>
    </sco:Collection>
  </TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>

  <!--
    ClassifyEmail workflow
    Inputs:  in_Subject (String), in_Body (String)
    Outputs: out_Category (String), out_Priority (String)

    Categories: "Billing", "Technical", "UrgentEscalation", "GeneralInquiry"
    Priorities:  "High", "Normal"

    Classification logic uses keyword matching on subject + body.
    Urgent/escalation keywords always override category to UrgentEscalation + High.
  -->
  <Sequence DisplayName="ClassifyEmail" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Sequence_1">
    <Sequence.Variables>
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="combinedText" />
    </Sequence.Variables>

    <!-- Step 1: Combine subject + body to a single lowercase string for matching -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Build combined text">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="combinedText" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="(If(in_Subject, "") & " " & If(in_Body, "")).ToLowerInvariant()" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <!-- Step 2: Default category = GeneralInquiry, priority = Normal -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set default category">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Category" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""GeneralInquiry"" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set default priority">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Priority" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""Normal"" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <!-- Step 3: Check for Billing keywords -->
    <If DisplayName="Check Billing Keywords">
      <If.Condition>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="combinedText.Contains("invoice") OrElse combinedText.Contains("payment") OrElse combinedText.Contains("charge") OrElse combinedText.Contains("billing") OrElse combinedText.Contains("refund") OrElse combinedText.Contains("subscription") OrElse combinedText.Contains("overcharged") OrElse combinedText.Contains("credit card") OrElse combinedText.Contains("receipt") OrElse combinedText.Contains("price")" />
        </InArgument>
      </If.Condition>
      <If.Then>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
          <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set Billing">
            <Assign.To>
              <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Category" />
              </OutArgument>
            </Assign.To>
            <Assign.Value>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""Billing"" />
              </InArgument>
            </Assign.Value>
          </Assign>
        </Sequence>
      </If.Then>
    </If>

    <!-- Step 4: Check for Technical keywords -->
    <If DisplayName="Check Technical Keywords">
      <If.Condition>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="combinedText.Contains("error") OrElse combinedText.Contains("bug") OrElse combinedText.Contains("crash") OrElse combinedText.Contains("broken") OrElse combinedText.Contains("not working") OrElse combinedText.Contains("technical") OrElse combinedText.Contains("issue") OrElse combinedText.Contains("problem") OrElse combinedText.Contains("support") OrElse combinedText.Contains("login") OrElse combinedText.Contains("password") OrElse combinedText.Contains("cannot access") OrElse combinedText.Contains("failed")" />
        </InArgument>
      </If.Condition>
      <If.Then>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
          <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set Technical">
            <Assign.To>
              <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Category" />
              </OutArgument>
            </Assign.To>
            <Assign.Value>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""Technical"" />
              </InArgument>
            </Assign.Value>
          </Assign>
        </Sequence>
      </If.Then>
    </If>

    <!-- Step 5: Check for Urgent/Escalation keywords — OVERRIDES everything above -->
    <If DisplayName="Check Urgent/Escalation Keywords">
      <If.Condition>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="combinedText.Contains("urgent") OrElse combinedText.Contains("escalate") OrElse combinedText.Contains("escalation") OrElse combinedText.Contains("immediately") OrElse combinedText.Contains("asap") OrElse combinedText.Contains("critical") OrElse combinedText.Contains("emergency") OrElse combinedText.Contains("lawsuit") OrElse combinedText.Contains("legal action") OrElse combinedText.Contains("unacceptable") OrElse combinedText.Contains("data loss") OrElse combinedText.Contains("account hacked")" />
        </InArgument>
      </If.Condition>
      <If.Then>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
          <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set UrgentEscalation">
            <Assign.To>
              <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Category" />
              </OutArgument>
            </Assign.To>
            <Assign.Value>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""UrgentEscalation"" />
              </InArgument>
            </Assign.Value>
          </Assign>
          <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Set High Priority">
            <Assign.To>
              <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="out_Priority" />
              </OutArgument>
            </Assign.To>
            <Assign.Value>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText=""High"" />
              </InArgument>
            </Assign.Value>
          </Assign>
        </Sequence>
      </If.Then>
    </If>

    <!-- Step 6: Log the classification result -->
    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Classification">
      <ui:LogMessage.Message>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Classified email — Subject: '{in_Subject}' → Category: {out_Category} | Priority: {out_Priority}"" />
        </InArgument>
      </ui:LogMessage.Message>
    </ui:LogMessage>

  </Sequence>
</Activity>

  <!--
    EmailSorter — Main orchestration workflow
    ==========================================
    1. Connects to your IMAP mailbox and fetches unread emails
    2. Loops over each email
       a. Invokes ClassifyEmail → determines Category + Priority
       b. Invokes RouteEmail    → moves the email to the correct IMAP subfolder
    3. Logs a summary when done

    Destination folders (created automatically by your mail client if absent):
      Support/Billing        — Billing / payment / invoice issues
      Support/Technical      — Bugs, errors, login problems, technical support
      Support/Urgent         — Escalations, emergencies, ASAP, legal threats
      Support/General        — Everything else / general inquiries

    Configuration:
      Pass in_IMAPServer, in_IMAPPort (usually 993), in_Email, in_Password via
      Orchestrator assets or input arguments when triggering this workflow.
      in_FetchFolder defaults to "Inbox"; in_TopMessages defaults to 30.
  -->
  <Sequence DisplayName="Main Sequence" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Sequence_1">
    <Sequence.Variables>
      <!-- List of retrieved emails -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="scg:List(sml:MailMessage)" Name="emailMessages" />
      <!-- Current email being processed in the loop -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" Name="currentEmail" />
      <!-- Classification outputs for the current email -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="emailCategory" />
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="emailPriority" />
      <!-- Running counter -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" Name="processedCount" Default="0" />
      <!-- Resolved fetch folder (in_FetchFolder or "Inbox") -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="fetchFolder" />
      <!-- Resolved top messages count (in_TopMessages or 30) -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" Name="topMessages" Default="30" />
    </Sequence.Variables>

    <!-- ── Init ── -->
    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Start">
      <ui:LogMessage.Message>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText=""EmailSorter started — fetching unread support emails..."" />
        </InArgument>
      </ui:LogMessage.Message>
    </ui:LogMessage>

    <!-- Resolve optional arguments: use provided values or sensible defaults -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Resolve fetch folder">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="fetchFolder" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="If(String.IsNullOrEmpty(in_FetchFolder), "Inbox", in_FetchFolder)" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Resolve top messages">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="topMessages" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="If(in_TopMessages > 0, in_TopMessages, 30)" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <!-- ── Step 1: Fetch unread emails from IMAP ── -->
    <TryCatch DisplayName="Try: Fetch Emails">
      <TryCatch.Try>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Try">
          <ui:GetIMAPMailMessages
            DisplayName="Get IMAP Emails"
            Email="[in_Email]"
            Password="[in_Password]"
            Server="[in_IMAPServer]"
            Port="[in_IMAPPort]"
            MailFolder="[fetchFolder]"
            OnlyUnreadMessages="True"
            MarkAsRead="True"
            Top="[topMessages]"
            OrderByDate="NewestFirst"
            SecureConnection="Auto"
            IgnoreCRL="False"
            UseOAuth="{x:Null}"
            ClientName="{x:Null}"
            ClientVersion="{x:Null}"
            UseISConnection="False"
            CreatedAfterSolutionSupport="True">
            <ui:GetIMAPMailMessages.Messages>
              <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="scg:List(sml:MailMessage)">
                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="scg:List(sml:MailMessage)" ExpressionText="emailMessages" />
              </OutArgument>
            </ui:GetIMAPMailMessages.Messages>
            <ui:GetIMAPMailMessages.ConnectionDetailsBackupSlot>
              <usau:BackupSlot x:TypeArguments="umae:ConnectionDetails" StoredValue="{x:Null}">
                <usau:BackupSlot.BackupValues>
                  <scg:Dictionary x:TypeArguments="umae:ConnectionDetails, scg:List(x:Object)" />
                </usau:BackupSlot.BackupValues>
              </usau:BackupSlot>
            </ui:GetIMAPMailMessages.ConnectionDetailsBackupSlot>
          </ui:GetIMAPMailMessages>

          <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Fetch Count">
            <ui:LogMessage.Message>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Fetched {If(emailMessages IsNot Nothing, emailMessages.Count, 0)} unread email(s) from {fetchFolder}"" />
              </InArgument>
            </ui:LogMessage.Message>
          </ui:LogMessage>
        </Sequence>
      </TryCatch.Try>
      <TryCatch.Catches>
        <Catch x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib">
          <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
            <ActivityAction.Argument>
              <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" Name="fetchException" />
            </ActivityAction.Argument>
            <Sequence DisplayName="Catch">
              <ui:LogMessage Level="Error" DisplayName="Log Fetch Error">
                <ui:LogMessage.Message>
                  <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
                    <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Failed to fetch emails: {fetchException.Message}"" />
                  </InArgument>
                </ui:LogMessage.Message>
              </ui:LogMessage>
              <Rethrow />
            </Sequence>
          </ActivityAction>
        </Catch>
      </TryCatch.Catches>
    </TryCatch>

    <!-- ── Step 2: Process each email — classify → route ── -->
    <If DisplayName="Any emails to process?">
      <If.Condition>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="emailMessages IsNot Nothing AndAlso emailMessages.Count > 0" />
        </InArgument>
      </If.Condition>
      <If.Then>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
          <ui:ForEach x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" DisplayName="For Each Email">
            <ui:ForEach.Values>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable" xmlns:sc="clr-namespace:System.Collections;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable" ExpressionText="emailMessages" />
              </InArgument>
            </ui:ForEach.Values>
            <ui:ForEach.Body>
              <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage">
                <ActivityAction.Argument>
                  <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" Name="emailItem" />
                </ActivityAction.Argument>
                <Sequence DisplayName="Body">

                  <!-- Assign current email for sub-workflows -->
                  <Assign x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" DisplayName="Set current email">
                    <Assign.To>
                      <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage">
                        <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" ExpressionText="currentEmail" />
                      </OutArgument>
                    </Assign.To>
                    <Assign.Value>
                      <InArgument x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage">
                        <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" ExpressionText="emailItem" />
                      </InArgument>
                    </Assign.Value>
                  </Assign>

                  <!-- TryCatch around each email so one failure doesn't stop the run -->
                  <TryCatch DisplayName="Try: Classify and Route">
                    <TryCatch.Try>
                      <Sequence DisplayName="Try">

                        <!-- 2a: Classify this email -->
                        <ui:InvokeWorkflowFile DisplayName="Classify Email" WorkflowFileName="Workflows\ClassifyEmail.xaml" UnSafe="False">
                          <ui:InvokeWorkflowFile.Arguments>
                            <scg:Dictionary x:TypeArguments="x:String, Argument">
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_Subject" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="If(currentEmail IsNot Nothing, currentEmail.Subject, "")" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_Body" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="If(currentEmail IsNot Nothing, currentEmail.Body, "")" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <OutArgument x:Key="out_Category" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="emailCategory" />
                              </OutArgument>
                              <OutArgument x:Key="out_Priority" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="emailPriority" />
                              </OutArgument>
                            </scg:Dictionary>
                          </ui:InvokeWorkflowFile.Arguments>
                        </ui:InvokeWorkflowFile>

                        <!-- 2b: Route this email to the right folder -->
                        <ui:InvokeWorkflowFile DisplayName="Route Email" WorkflowFileName="Workflows\RouteEmail.xaml" UnSafe="False">
                          <ui:InvokeWorkflowFile.Arguments>
                            <scg:Dictionary x:TypeArguments="x:String, Argument">
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_MailMessage" x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="sml:MailMessage" ExpressionText="currentEmail" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_Category" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="emailCategory" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_IMAPServer" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="in_IMAPServer" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_IMAPPort" x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="in_IMAPPort" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_Email" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="in_Email" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_Password" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="in_Password" />
                              </InArgument>
                              <InArgument x:Key="in_FromFolder" x:TypeArguments="x:String">
                                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="fetchFolder" />
                              </InArgument>
                            </scg:Dictionary>
                          </ui:InvokeWorkflowFile.Arguments>
                        </ui:InvokeWorkflowFile>

                        <!-- Increment counter -->
                        <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Increment counter">
                          <Assign.To>
                            <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
                              <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="processedCount" />
                            </OutArgument>
                          </Assign.To>
                          <Assign.Value>
                            <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
                              <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="processedCount + 1" />
                            </InArgument>
                          </Assign.Value>
                        </Assign>

                      </Sequence>
                    </TryCatch.Try>
                    <TryCatch.Catches>
                      <Catch x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib">
                        <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
                          <ActivityAction.Argument>
                            <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" Name="emailException" />
                          </ActivityAction.Argument>
                          <Sequence DisplayName="Catch">
                            <ui:LogMessage Level="Warn" DisplayName="Log Email Error">
                              <ui:LogMessage.Message>
                                <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
                                  <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Failed to classify/route email '{If(currentEmail IsNot Nothing, currentEmail.Subject, "(unknown)")}': {emailException.Message} — skipping."" />
                                </InArgument>
                              </ui:LogMessage.Message>
                            </ui:LogMessage>
                          </Sequence>
                        </ActivityAction>
                      </Catch>
                    </TryCatch.Catches>
                  </TryCatch>

                </Sequence>
              </ActivityAction>
            </ui:ForEach.Body>
          </ui:ForEach>
        </Sequence>
      </If.Then>
      <If.Else>
        <Sequence DisplayName="Else">
          <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log No Emails">
            <ui:LogMessage.Message>
              <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText=""No unread emails found. Nothing to process."" />
              </InArgument>
            </ui:LogMessage.Message>
          </ui:LogMessage>
        </Sequence>
      </If.Else>
    </If>

    <!-- ── Step 3: Write final summary ── -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Set out_ProcessedCount">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="out_ProcessedCount" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="processedCount" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Summary">
      <ui:LogMessage.Message>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"EmailSorter finished. Processed {processedCount} email(s)."" />
        </InArgument>
      </ui:LogMessage.Message>
    </ui:LogMessage>

  </Sequence>
</Activity>

# UiPath Mail Activities

`UiPath.Mail.Activities`

Send, receive, and manage email messages across multiple protocols: SMTP, IMAP, POP3, Exchange (EWS), and Outlook (COM). Includes triggers for new email events, attachment handling, and message operations (move, delete, mark as read).

## Documentation

- [XAML Activities Reference](activities/) — Per-activity documentation for XAML workflows
- [Coded Workflow API Reference](coded/coded-api.md) — Service API for coded C# workflows (`mail.Smtp(...)`, `mail.Imap(...)`, `mail.Pop3(...)`)
- [Type Reference](activities/types/) — Output and input model types (MailMessage, UiPathMailMessage, MailEventInfo)
- [Filter Reference](activities/filtering/) — Mail filter collections (MailFilterArgument, TriggerMailFilterCollection)

## Activities

### SMTP (Cross-platform)

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [Send SMTP Email](activities/SendMail.md) | Send an email message using SMTP protocol |

### IMAP (Cross-platform)

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [Get IMAP Email List](activities/GetIMAPMailMessages.md) | Retrieve email messages from an IMAP server |
| [Move IMAP Email](activities/MoveIMAPMailMessageToFolder.md) | Move an email to a different folder on an IMAP server |
| [Delete IMAP Email](activities/DeleteImapMailMessage.md) | Delete an email from an IMAP server |
| [IMAP Email Received](activities/NewIMAPEmailReceivedTrigger.md) | Trigger when a new email is received via IMAP |

### POP3 (Cross-platform)

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [Get POP3 Email List](activities/GetPOP3MailMessages.md) | Retrieve email messages from a POP3 server |

### Outlook (Windows only)

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [Send Outlook Email](activities/SendOutlookMail.md) | Send an email using Outlook |
| [Get Outlook Email List](activities/GetOutlookMailMessages.md) | Retrieve email messages from Outlook |
| [Reply to Outlook Email](activities/ReplyToOutlookMailMessage.md) | Reply to an Outlook email message |
| [Mark Outlook Email as Read](activities/MarkOutlookMailAsRead.md) | Mark an Outlook email as read or unread |
| [Set Outlook Email Categories](activities/SetOutlookMailCategories.md) | Set categories on an Outlook email |
| [Delete Outlook Email](activities/DeleteOutlookMailMessage.md) | Delete an email from Outlook |
| [Save Outlook Email](activities/SaveOutlookMailMessage.md) | Save an Outlook email to disk |
| [Move Outlook Email](activities/MoveOutlookMessage.md) | Move an Outlook email to a different folder |
| [Outlook Email Received](activities/OutlookMailMessagesTrigger.md) | Trigger when a new email is received in Outlook |

### Exchange EWS (Windows only)

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [Exchange Scope](activities/ExchangeScope.md) | Establish an Exchange connection for child activities |
| [Send Exchange Email](activities/SendExchangeMail.md) | Send an email using Exchange Web Services |
| [Get Exchange Email List](activities/GetExchangeMailMessages.md) | Retrieve email messages from Exchange |
| [Create Draft](activities/CreateDraft.md) | Create a draft email in Exchange |
| [Delete Exchange Email](activities/DeleteMail.md) | Delete an email from Exchange |
| [Move Exchange Email](activities/MoveMessageToFolder.md) | Move an email to a folder in Exchange |

1	# UiPathMailMessage
2	
3	`UiPath.Mail.UiPathMailMessage`
4	
5	A cross-platform email message that extends System.Net.Mail.MailMessage. This type is used by newer Mail activities and provides the same properties as MailMessage with display ordering and category metadata for the UiPath designer.
6	
7	Inherits all properties from [MailMessage](MailMessage.md).
8	
9	## Simplified Properties
10	
11	These properties are re-declared with `[Category(PropertyCategory.Simplified)]` for designer display ordering. They delegate to the base MailMessage implementation.
12	
13	| Name | Type | Description |
14	|------|------|-------------|
15	| To | MailAddressCollection | The recipients of the email. (Order 1) |
16	| From | MailAddress | The sender's email address. (Order 2) |
17	| ReplyToList | MailAddressCollection | The list of reply-to addresses. (Order 3) |
18	| Body | string | The body content of the email. (Order 4) |
19	| Subject | string | The subject line of the email. (Order 5) |

<Activity mc:Ignorable="sap sap2010" x:Class="Main"
  mva:VisualBasic.Settings="{x:Null}"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
  xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
  xmlns:mva="clr-namespace:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities;assembly=System.Activities"
  xmlns:sap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sap2010="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=mscorlib"
  xmlns:scg="clr-namespace:System.Collections.Generic;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"
  xmlns:sml="clr-namespace:System.Net.Mail;assembly=System.Net.Mail"
  xmlns:upm="clr-namespace:UiPath.Mail;assembly=UiPath.Mail.Activities"
  xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"

  xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml">
  <x:Members>
    <x:Property Name="in_IMAPServer" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_IMAPPort" Type="InArgument(x:Int32)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_Email" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_Password" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_FetchFolder" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
    <x:Property Name="in_TopMessages" Type="InArgument(x:Int32)" />
    <x:Property Name="out_ProcessedCount" Type="OutArgument(x:Int32)" />
  </x:Members>
  <TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="x:String">
      <x:String>System.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Statements</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Expressions</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Validation</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.XamlIntegration</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections.Generic</x:String>

      <x:String>UiPath.Core</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Core.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Windows.Markup</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Mail.Activities.Enums</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Mail</x:String>
    </sco:Collection>
  </TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
  <TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="AssemblyReference">

      <AssemblyReference>System.Xml</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Xml.Linq</AssemblyReference>

      <AssemblyReference>UiPath.System.Activities</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>UiPath.UiAutomation.Activities</AssemblyReference>
